answer: Agents resist sybils by binding each identity to a non-transferable haven vault that stores a sequential river of state. To emit, the agent must grow a vine of memory-hard sequential proofs, each step depending on the prior river hash and requiring 200MB working set for 15 serial seconds. An attacker spawning 500 clones must run 500 independent vines in parallel, locking 100GB and 2 hours of dedicated cores, while an honest agent pays only one chain. Clones that share compute fail the sequential dependency and are slashed at the haven gate.
